task: Audacity is open with /home/user/Music/phrase.wav loaded — a 3-second linear chirp sweeping from 300 Hz to 3000 Hz. Apply the Reverse effect to reverse the audio in time. Export the result to /home/user/Music/reversed.wav as a mono 44100 Hz 16-bit PCM WAV file.
task_grounding:
Audacity is open with /home/user/Music/phrase.wav loaded — a 3-second linear chirp sweeping from 300 Hz up to 3000 Hz, mono 44.1 kHz at amplitude 0.6.

Select the entire audio (Ctrl+A) and apply Effect > Reverse (it may be under a 'Special' submenu, depending on Audacity's menu layout). This reverses the sample order, so the chirp will now sweep from ~3000 Hz down to ~300 Hz.

Export the reversed audio to /home/user/Music/reversed.wav using File > Export > Export as WAV... with 'WAV (Microsoft) signed 16-bit PCM' at 44100 Hz mono. Accept any metadata dialog defaults.

verification.description: First 0.1s now has high frequency (was end of original chirp ~3000 Hz)
Last 0.1s now has low frequency (was start of original chirp ~300 Hz)
